class: A one-row dashboard action paid a full engine construction plus a full page render, so 'Not interested' took the better part of a second
fix: The dismiss route uses a new light dismiss_discovered_job (one UPDATE, no profile, no resume) and answers JSON to fetch requests while the plain form still redirects; cockpit.js removes the card in place, announces it, and reloads only on failure. The index lists the tracker once (shared through Flask's request store), _current_runs returns early with no runs, and process liveness is cached 10s per pid instead of spawning tasklist per run per page.
prevention: Single-row actions answer without engine construction and without a full render; page loads list shared state once per request and never spawn a process per row per load.
root_cause: POST /api/discovered/<id>/dismiss built a whole JobDiscoveryEngine (profile, resume) for one UPDATE, then 302-redirected to a full index render that listed the tracker twice, reconciled runs, and spawned tasklist once per live run (measured 0.77s, 0.43s in _current_runs).
site: Suggested-jobs 'Not interested' button, web_ui.py + job_discovery.py + static/cockpit.js, 3 November 2026
symptom: Clicking 'Not interested' on a suggested job took a lot of time: the click stalled, then the whole page reloaded to show one card gone.
why_tests_missed: Dashboard tests rendered pages with mocked trackers and never timed or counted the work behind one click; no test posted to the dismiss route at all.
